reverse_dcf_check: 22.8x NTM earnings at the horizon (a 4.4% earnings yield) implies, at a ~9% cost of equity and high cash payout, roughly 5% perpetual EPS growth after 2028 with GAAP EBIT margins held near 18.5-19%: plausible for an HVAC leader with a 52%-of-revenue backlog and services ~1/3 of revenue, but it leaves no room for a margin step-down in a data-center downturn.

reasoning: Started from the filings: Q3 2026 beat on revenue (+18%, organic +16%) and bookings (+21%), backlog $12.5B (+73%, ~$1B acquired Stellar), but the reaffirmed EPS guide implies Q4 3.41-3.51 vs Street 3.59 and margins slipped (gross -160bp, EMEA -240bp, APAC -390bp, pricing +0.6%): the market sold the margin, not the demand. Lane evidence: CBRE/JLL show record data-center construction (7.5 GW in CBRE primary markets, 66 GW per JLL, vacancy ~1%, tenants contracting for 2028), but CBRE H2 2025 also showed the first construction decline since 2020 on power and permits; Moody's sees hyperscaler capex near $1T in 2027. Trade press (ACHR) confirms applied bookings +120% and no 2026 residential price increase; capacity additions (Grand Rapids doubling air-cooled chillers, Fort Smith AHUs) support ~12% volume growth; forum anecdotes show Trane lead times >6 months vs Daikin 2 months (share risk, single undated source, not used in numbers); Form 4 data shows CEO selling ~$44M and no buys. Build: bookings dip ~2% in 2027 against tough comps, revenue converts the backlog at capacity pace (+12% 2027, +7% 2028), margins recover only ~50bp in 2027, giving FY2027 EPS ~18.0 (Street 17.71, whisper 18.10) and FY2028 ~19.9 (Street 20.41, ours -2.5% as growth normalises). Valued with the k=0.8 shrink on a 7-peer HVAC median (21.8x) less 0.5x for post-horizon data-center and technology risk. Downside and upside move bookings and margins as the playbook says, with multiple shifts of -3.5/+3.5 turns; the left tail is fatter (side vols ~0.33 down vs ~0.22 up). Limits: X/Twitter not fetched; no prediction-market price found for a 2027 recession contract (none quoted); in-lane share of sources ~49% because the guidance record needs 13 company filings.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set (6 drivers: bookings, backlog, international revenue, Americas and international GAAP margins, corporate cost). Americas revenue = 0.985 x (bookings - change in backlog) - International: the playbook backlog-burn build. Two segments (Americas; EMEA+APAC combined as International) to stay within 6 drivers. Value is carried by a P/E (NTM at the horizon, weight 0.75) on the build's own NOPAT, and a trailing GAAP EV/EBITDA cross-check (0.25, thin peer set). No DCF (policy); no SOTP (TT is one HVAC business). Leg weights are judgment within the playbook (forward earnings most accurate). Driven share of revenue 100%; base-year residual +1.6% (Americas from bookings/backlog vs reported).
model_inputs.gap_note: Q1 2026 actual backlog jump includes ~$1B acquired Stellar backlog (bookings - change in backlog does not reproduce Q1 2026 revenue); forecasts unaffected. Americas margin driver uses agg mean rather than revenue weight (the weight would be an expression with p_bl). No financing event: none >= 20% probability (TT funds buybacks and bolt-ons from FCF; $3.4B authorisation left). Model EPS excludes NCI (~$25M/yr) and other income. Research leg in-lane share ~49%: the guidance record needed 13 company filings.
